# Refusal and unsupported codes

A refusal reports a violation of the [specification](../../spec/format-1.md) or an unsupported dataset version.
The codes are stable; the text of an error is not ([§10](../../spec/format-1.md#10-refusal-codes)).
The source of this page is [spec/refusal-codes.json](../../spec/refusal-codes.json), plus the causes and actions in [docs/data/refusal-actions.json](../data/refusal-actions.json).

"Detected" is the latest point at which a reader must detect the fault. A reader may detect it earlier.

## Refusal codes

| Code | Meaning | Detected | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`no_manifest`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#no_manifest) | The dataset root has no manifest.json. | open | Check the path points at the directory or prefix that holds manifest.json. If a producer is still writing, wait for its commit. |
| [`invalid_manifest`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#invalid_manifest) | The manifest is not valid: unparseable JSON, duplicate member names (including inside extensions), a missing, extra or ill-typed member, an extensions member that is not an object, a wrong format name, malformed base64, a part with no rows, or a part path that breaks PART-1. Also part bounds in the manifest that are not ascending and disjoint (PART-4). A missing or malformed key declaration is also invalid_manifest. | open | Check the manifest against spec/manifest.schema.json, then the rules of §3. The error detail may identify a member or describe a manifest-wide parsing problem. |
| [`unsupported_version`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#unsupported_version) | The manifest's format_version and draft_revision pair is not one the reader supports. | open | Use a reader release that supports the dataset's version pair, or rewrite the dataset with a producer of this reader's version. |
| [`missing_part`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#missing_part) | A part the manifest lists does not exist. | first touch of the part | Restore the part, or rewrite the dataset. A producer must make every part durable before it commits the manifest (COMMIT-1). |
| [`part_mismatch`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#part_mismatch) | A part's size in bytes, or its footer's row count, differs from its manifest entry. | first touch of the part | Treat the dataset as damaged and rewrite it. Parts are immutable once committed (COMMIT-2); a producer records each part's size and rows from the sealed file. |
| [`invalid_footer`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#invalid_footer) | A part is shorter than 12 bytes, has invalid magic under CHECK-1 after applying its encryption classification, its Parquet footer cannot be read, its row groups' row counts do not sum to the footer's row count, or a column chunk refers to another file (file_path set). Also a recognized leaf annotation that violates Parquet physical-type or parameter restrictions, including missing parameters or empty required unions, on any leaf (even unprojected). | first touch of the part | Compare the part's size and checksum with the source. Copy parts whole and only after they are complete. |
| [`stamp_mismatch`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#stamp_mismatch) | A part's seekparquet.* footer metadata is missing, duplicated, forbidden (a draft_revision stamp on a non-draft file), without a value, not canonical, or different from the manifest. | first touch of the part | Write the stamps into the part's footer key-value metadata (STAMP-1), exactly as the manifest states the version, schema id and key. See the producing guide. |
| [`invalid_key_column`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#invalid_key_column) | A part has no top-level REQUIRED BYTE_ARRAY column named by manifest key.column, the key column carries an annotation other than STRING or UTF8, or column_orders does not give it TYPE_ORDER. | first touch of the part | Declare the key a non-nullable binary or string column (Parquet REQUIRED BYTE_ARRAY) with column_orders set (KEY-1, KEY-5). |
| [`inconsistent_column`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#inconsistent_column) | A column appears in several parts with different physical types, repetition or nesting. | first touch of the part | Write every part with one schema. A part may omit a column (COL-2), but a column it has must match the other parts. |
| [`missing_sorting_columns`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#missing_sorting_columns) | A non-empty row group does not declare key ascending as its first sorting column. | first touch of the part | Declare the key as the first sorting column, ascending, on every non-empty row group (RG-1). In pyarrow: sorting_columns=[pq.SortingColumn(i)]. |
| [`missing_page_index`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#missing_page_index) | A non-empty row group's key column lacks a ColumnIndex or an OffsetIndex. | read | Enable the page index for the key column (RG-2). In pyarrow: write_page_index=True. |
| [`invalid_page_index`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#invalid_page_index) | A key column's page index is inconsistent with itself or with the physical pages: list lengths differ, a null page, an empty list, row positions or locations out of range, an entry that does not locate exactly one data page, a page whose row count differs from its indexed interval, a bound that is not valid UTF-8 where KEY-6 applies, or decoded keys outside the page's bounds. For an indexed key page this includes failure to decode a complete header, a non-data page, or a valid header whose extent or declared row count disagrees with its index; intrinsic header corruption takes precedence under CHECK-5. | read | Rewrite the part with a writer whose bounds hold every key of the page (RG-5). Validate at the profile level to detect invalid key-page bounds; validation stops when it encounters a fault. |
| [`invalid_key`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#invalid_key) | An empty key, or a key that is not valid UTF-8 in a key column annotated STRING or UTF8. | read | Drop or encode empty keys before writing (KEY-2). Store keys that are not UTF-8 in an unannotated binary key column (KEY-6). |
| [`key_order`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#key_order) | Keys decrease within a page or across pages, row groups or parts, or equal keys appear when manifest key.unique is true. | read | Sort keys by unsigned byte order (KEY-3), and declare key.unique false when keys repeat. |
| [`invalid_parquet`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#invalid_parquet) | Corruption in the Parquet data itself: a page that does not decompress or decode, a malformed dictionary, or a value count that does not match the rows. Decoded page headers with negative counts or sizes or invalid V2 level lengths retain this code even on an indexed key page (CHECK-5 precedence). | validation, full level | Rewrite or restore the part. Validate at the full level to check all stored columns. A failed run reports the fault encountered, not every damaged page. |
| [`bounds_mismatch`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#bounds_mismatch) | A part's actual first or last key differs from its manifest bounds. | validation, profile level | Write the manifest's bounds from the first and last keys actually written to each part (PART-3). |
| [`digest_mismatch`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#digest_mismatch) | A part's sha256 differs from the manifest's. | validation, digest level | Treat the part as damaged and restore or rewrite it. Compute the digest over the sealed file's bytes. |

## Unsupported codes

An unsupported code reports a feature the reader does not implement. It does not certify the dataset’s validity; the reader may stop before checking other rules.

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| [`unsupported_encoding`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#unsupported_encoding) | a codec or encoding outside what the reader implements (never one of the ENC-1 baseline; for example BROTLI); includes unrecognized numeric Encoding/CompressionCodec values only when the request needs that data (ENC-1) | Inspect the error detail to identify the unsupported codec or encoding, then rewrite the affected column using a supported codec and encoding, preferably the ENC-1 baseline. An unprojected value column’s unsupported encoding or codec does not itself block the request. |
| [`unsupported_projection`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#unsupported_projection) | a request to project a nested or repeated column | Project only top-level, non-repeated columns (COL-3), or read the part with a general Parquet reader. |
| [`unsupported_encryption`](../guides/troubleshooting.md#unsupported_encryption) | an encrypted part: PARE magic at either end of a part of at least 12 bytes (CHECK-1), or readable footer metadata declaring encryption (FILE-2) | Read the part with a Parquet reader that decrypts, or write the dataset unencrypted (FILE-2). |

## Codes in Go and Java

Go reports a refusal as a `*RefusalError` whose `Code` is a `RefusalCode`; `RefusalCodeOf(err)` returns it. Java throws a `RefusalException` whose `code()` is a `RefusalCode`. Unsupported features are Go `*UnsupportedError` and Java `UnsupportedFeatureException`, each with an `UnsupportedCode`.

| Code | Go constant | Java constant | Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_manifest` | `CodeNoManifest` | `RefusalCode.NO_MANIFEST` | [LAYOUT-1](../../spec/format-1.md#layout-1) |
| `invalid_manifest` | `CodeInvalidManifest` | `RefusalCode.INVALID_MANIFEST` | [MAN-1](../../spec/format-1.md#man-1), [MAN-2](../../spec/format-1.md#man-2), [MAN-3](../../spec/format-1.md#man-3), [MAN-4](../../spec/format-1.md#man-4), [PART-1](../../spec/format-1.md#part-1), [PART-2](../../spec/format-1.md#part-2), [PART-3](../../spec/format-1.md#part-3), [MAN-6](../../spec/format-1.md#man-6), [MAN-7](../../spec/format-1.md#man-7), [PART-4](../../spec/format-1.md#part-4), [MAN-8](../../spec/format-1.md#man-8), [EXT-4](../../spec/format-1.md#ext-4) |
| `unsupported_version` | `CodeUnsupportedVersion` | `RefusalCode.UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` | [MAN-4](../../spec/format-1.md#man-4), [MAN-5](../../spec/format-1.md#man-5), [VER-1](../../spec/format-1.md#ver-1) |
| `missing_part` | `CodeMissingPart` | `RefusalCode.MISSING_PART` | [LAYOUT-1](../../spec/format-1.md#layout-1), [CHECK-1](../../spec/format-1.md#check-1) |
| `part_mismatch` | `CodePartMismatch` | `RefusalCode.PART_MISMATCH` | [CHECK-1](../../spec/format-1.md#check-1) |
| `invalid_footer` | `CodeInvalidFooter` | `RefusalCode.INVALID_FOOTER` | [CHECK-1](../../spec/format-1.md#check-1), [FILE-1](../../spec/format-1.md#file-1) |
| `stamp_mismatch` | `CodeStampMismatch` | `RefusalCode.STAMP_MISMATCH` | [STAMP-1](../../spec/format-1.md#stamp-1), [STAMP-2](../../spec/format-1.md#stamp-2) |
| `invalid_key_column` | `CodeInvalidKeyColumn` | `RefusalCode.INVALID_KEY_COLUMN` | [KEY-1](../../spec/format-1.md#key-1), [KEY-5](../../spec/format-1.md#key-5) |
| `inconsistent_column` | `CodeInconsistentColumn` | `RefusalCode.INCONSISTENT_COLUMN` | [COL-5](../../spec/format-1.md#col-5) |
| `missing_sorting_columns` | `CodeMissingSortingColumns` | `RefusalCode.MISSING_SORTING_COLUMNS` | [RG-1](../../spec/format-1.md#rg-1) |
| `missing_page_index` | `CodeMissingPageIndex` | `RefusalCode.MISSING_PAGE_INDEX` | [RG-2](../../spec/format-1.md#rg-2), [RG-7](../../spec/format-1.md#rg-7) |
| `invalid_page_index` | `CodeInvalidPageIndex` | `RefusalCode.INVALID_PAGE_INDEX` | [RG-3](../../spec/format-1.md#rg-3), [RG-4](../../spec/format-1.md#rg-4), [RG-5](../../spec/format-1.md#rg-5), [RG-7](../../spec/format-1.md#rg-7), [KEY-6](../../spec/format-1.md#key-6), [CHECK-5](../../spec/format-1.md#check-5) |
| `invalid_key` | `CodeInvalidKey` | `RefusalCode.INVALID_KEY` | [KEY-2](../../spec/format-1.md#key-2), [KEY-6](../../spec/format-1.md#key-6) |
| `key_order` | `CodeKeyOrder` | `RefusalCode.KEY_ORDER` | [KEY-3](../../spec/format-1.md#key-3) |
| `invalid_parquet` | `CodeInvalidParquet` | `RefusalCode.INVALID_PARQUET` | [CHECK-5](../../spec/format-1.md#check-5) |
| `bounds_mismatch` | `CodeBoundsMismatch` | `RefusalCode.BOUNDS_MISMATCH` | [PART-3](../../spec/format-1.md#part-3), [PART-4](../../spec/format-1.md#part-4) |
| `digest_mismatch` | `CodeDigestMismatch` | `RefusalCode.DIGEST_MISMATCH` | [PART-5](../../spec/format-1.md#part-5) |
| `unsupported_encoding` | `UnsupportedEncoding` | `UnsupportedCode.ENCODING` | |
| `unsupported_projection` | `UnsupportedProjection` | `UnsupportedCode.PROJECTION` | |
| `unsupported_encryption` | `UnsupportedEncryption` | `UnsupportedCode.ENCRYPTION` | |

## Outcomes that are not codes

| Outcome | Meaning | Go | Java |
|---|---|---|---|
| invalid_request | The request itself is malformed: a limit that is not a positive integer, a delimiter that is not one byte, malformed base64, a malformed cursor, a prefix cursor in a range request. | `ErrInvalidRequest` | `IllegalArgumentException` |
| unsupported | A needed feature is unsupported; the dataset may be valid. Unrecognized numeric encoding/codec values follow ENC-1 without certifying validity. | `*UnsupportedError` | `UnsupportedFeatureException` |
| error | Anything else, such as a failure to read storage. Not a statement about the data. | the `Source`'s error, `ErrClosed`, or the context's error | `StorageException`, `IllegalStateException`, or `CancellationException` |

A limit exceeded is none of these: see [limits](limits.md).
